units.summary: New test. After CompactSelectedSeries evicts a non-stale series, it forces a WAL checkpoint with a mint inside the head range and checks that the evicted series's label record is still in the checkpoint. It changes no production code, so a line-by-line review isn't needed.
units.headline: New test: evicted selected series record survives WAL checkpoint
units.reason: New test only; it cannot affect production behavior.

units.summary: gcStaleSeries is generalised into gcSeries, which takes a shouldEvict predicate. numStaleSeries is now reduced only by the number of deleted series that were actually stale, not by every deleted series. Before, the two counts were equal because only stale series were deleted. Now that non-stale series can be evicted, using the old count would have pushed the gauge below its true value.
units.headline: Head GC takes eviction predicate; stale counter counts only stale deletions
units.reason: Changes the eviction logic and head series counters that many paths rely on.
focus: numStaleSeries is reduced only when the deleted series is stale, matching how other GC paths do it (head.go lines 1831 and 2367)
tombstones and WAL expiries are recorded for every deleted ref, including non-stale ones

units.summary: The hardcoded staleness check is replaced by the caller's shouldEvict predicate, which runs under the series lock after the maxTime guard. Deleted series that are stale are counted for the gauge using isStaleSeries. The stale-only eviction path keeps its old behavior because its predicate still includes isStaleSeries.
units.headline: stripeSeries GC uses caller predicate and counts stale deletions
units.reason: Eviction is now decided by the caller-supplied predicate, so non-stale series can be removed from the head.
focus: shouldEvict runs while series.Lock is held; hasAppendIDAbove requires that lock
truncateStaleSeries still evicts only stale series because its predicate includes isStaleSeries
